newsitem.title: UK: High-speed gel promises life-like prosthetics.
newsitem.headline: High-speed gel promises life-like prosthetics.

text.p: American scientists said on Thursday they had developed a polymer gel that responds to electric impulses just as fast as human muscles, raising hopes that prosthetic limbs could soon be as good as the real thing.
In experiments, tiny flags attached to electrodes embedded in the gel were made to wave almost instantaneously when an electric current was applied.

Conducting substances previously tested by robotics researchers took at least three seconds to respond to an electric impulse, whereas human skeletal muscles take 100 milliseconds to react after receiving an electrical signal from a nerve.

The scientists at New York's Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute said their gel, made by by blending electrorheological fluids with elastic polymer, responds to electric impulses just as quickly as human muscles.
"We applied a 1-hertz AC electric field and in less than 100 milliseconds, the gel began to compress," Katherine Bonsor of the research institute, told New Scientist magazine.
She said the robotics industry had shown an interest in the gel because it gives fast, smooth responses, and unlike mechanical devices, it can be made very small.
But more study is needed before the gels can be used to maneouvre prosthetic limbs because of the high voltage they require.
